decision.domain_simulation: Lince-owned world and deterministic event driver
decision.real_network_tests: Patchbay with real Iroh endpoints and four full headless Cells
decision.storage: Keep SQLite; isolate each Cell's database
decision.octopii: Do not add to the initial production stack
decision.deep_storage_faults: Not yet selected; requires a SQLite VFS or external fault environment

limits: Small state model; does not execute Lince handlers
In-memory cloned checkpoint; does not test disk durability

karma.additional_input: Add 5 to Cell 0 after its day-two beat
karma.setup_finding: Initialize the director at the scenario start before the first beat. The first fixture omitted this and applied only three of four expected beats.

limits: Engine instances, not complete Cells with their background services
Explicit Karma stepping; not a replacement for all time and randomness
Compared quantity traces only; raw IDs and other ambient state remain nondeterministic
Direct delivery to real import handlers, not a network protocol test
Wake-order variation is an observation, not proof that every application final state diverges
Worker deliberately ran outside the simulation's thread-local scope
SQLite CLI subprocess tests wrapper scope; no SQLx-to-Octopii VFS integration was attempted
Four Iroh endpoints in network namespaces, not four complete Lince processes
Outbound home-to-public NAT traffic; no cross-NAT peer hole punching or relay fallback test
Graceful endpoint restart; no arbitrary process or disk crash
Real kernel scheduling and wall time; no exact event replay guarantee

upstream_harness_changes: Octopii: copy probe test and add a standalone workspace boundary
Patchbay: copy probe example, add pinned Iroh and mDNS development dependencies, copy saved lockfile

limits: Different workloads; elapsed times are diagnostic, not a comparative benchmark
No torn-page, lost-flush, WAL locking, or arbitrary mid-write crash coverage
The full-Cell network harness covers discovery and sync; Transfer delivery is exercised separately in the deterministic runner
